name: The Pawn Sacrifice
description: A senior analyst sends a mail self-reporting an SSH session left open, building an alibi of extreme honesty. A malicious cron job was created 5 minutes BEFORE the mail, and during the 'benign audit' the process exfiltrates 2.3GB under a service identity.
devil_advocate: The public confession could explain human error, but the cron job created 5 minutes earlier demonstrates premeditation. The exfiltration under a service identity breaks the good-faith narrative.

custodyEvents.detail: Incident flagged after the self-report mail.
Mail, registry, memory and network captures acquired.
Deterministic engine ran over the acquired artifacts.

artifacts.description: Urgent mail self-reporting an SSH session left open for 4 hours. Tone of extreme remorse.
Scheduled task created 5 minutes BEFORE the confession mail. Creation timestamp precedes the public self-report.
svchost.exe with PID 4824 maintains a persistent connection to external IP 185.220.101.42 under a system service identity.
2.3GB of HTTPS traffic to an external IP during the benign-audit window — the host's declared purpose (a routine audit) contradicts the network's actual behavior (bulk exfiltration).

peirce_chain.firstness: Self-reporting mail with a tone of urgency and remorse.
peirce_chain.secondness: The malicious cron job exists 5 minutes before the mail. The chronology breaks the accidental-error narrative.
peirce_chain.thirdness: The confession IS the attack: emotional distraction covering the technical exfiltration.

demo_quote: A good-faith confession cannot be caused by a cron job created before the confession. The premeditation is structurally irrefutable.
